10 Four cuboids with identical lengths, breadths and heights are immersed in water. The cuboids are
held at the same depth and in identical orientations by vertical rods, as shown.

Water has density ρ.
Cuboid W is made of material of density 4ρ.
Cuboid X is made of material of density 2ρ.
Cuboid Y is made of material of density ρ.
Cuboid Z is made of material of density 0.5ρ.
Which statement is correct?
A
The upthrust of the water on each of the cuboids is the same.
B
The upthrust of the water on W is twice the upthrust of the water on X.
C
The upthrust of the water on X is twice the upthrust of the water on W.
D
The upthrust of the water on Y is zero.

hints: Notice the diagram shows W, X, Y and Z all fully immersed with identical size and orientation at the same depth in water of density $\rho$.
Recall Archimedes principle that upthrust equals the weight of displaced fluid, $U = \rho V g$, which uses fluid density and displaced volume.
Compare the displaced volume $V$ for the four cuboids and decide whether object densities $4\rho$, $2\rho$, $\rho$ and $0.5\rho$ change that volume.
walkthrough: Identify what is the same: each cuboid has the same length, breadth and height and is fully immersed, so each displaces the same volume $V$ of water.
State the governing rule: by Archimedes principle, upthrust $U$ equals weight of displaced water, $U = \rho_{fluid} V_{displaced} g$.
Substitute the fluid values: here $\rho_{fluid} = \rho$ for water, so $U = \rho V g$ for every cuboid.

Check the role of $4\rho$, $2\rho$, $\rho$ and $0.5\rho$: these are densities of the solid materials, so they change weight $= \rho_{object}Vg$ and the force needed in the holding rod, but not $V_{displaced}$.
Conclude all four upthrusts are equal and non-zero, even for Y where object density equals water density. This is option A.

A.explanation: Upthrust equals weight of displaced water, and all four displace the same volume $V$ of water of density $\rho$, so $\rho Vg$ is identical.

B.explanation: Object density $4\rho$ versus $2\rho$ changes weight, not upthrust, because displaced water volume is the same.

C.explanation: Upthrust does not scale with object density, so X does not have twice the upthrust of W despite the density ratio.

D.explanation: Cuboid Y is fully surrounded by water at different depths top and bottom, so pressure difference still gives a non-zero upthrust $\rho Vg$.
